title: Sukhothai Kingdom

endonym.native: อาณาจักรสุโขทัย

capsule: The Sukhothai Kingdom was established around 1238–1240 when local Thai chieftains Si Inthrathit and Pha Muang revolted against Khmer garrisons and founded an independent polity in the upper Chao Phraya basin of north-central Thailand. It reached its greatest extent under Ramkhamhaeng the Great (r. c. 1279–1298), who extended suzerainty southward to the Malay Peninsula and northward toward Lan Na, and who is traditionally credited with devising the Thai script (1283 inscription). Sukhothai was a notable center of Theravada Buddhist patronage, producing a distinctive school of Buddha imagery; after Ramkhamhaeng's death the kingdom contracted as subordinate principalities reasserted independence. By 1378 Sukhothai had become a vassal of the rising Ayutthaya Kingdom, which formally annexed it in 1438, with our dataset's terminus of 1458 reflecting the complete administrative absorption of its remaining territories.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Sukhothai heartland is archaeologically well-documented; the peripheral extent under Ramkhamhaeng is based primarily on the 1283 Ramkhamhaeng inscription, whose authenticity has been debated, making the maximal territorial polygon speculative.
